title: SF1116 (2023-2024 Regular): Criminal background checks requirement for firearms transfers

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (1st Engrossment, 2023-03-27; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/93/2023/0/SF/1116/versions/1/)
provenance.note: Other: 1st Engrossment, 2023-03-27; official copy from revisor.mn.gov. Differs from the as-filed SF 1175 text: adds a criminal-gang-database ground for denial, a 30-day waiting period and 30-day permit decision, a de novo court appeal with a clear-and-convincing burden on the sheriff, a dealer-facilitated transfer path, a 10-year record retention and a misdemeanor (not gross misdemeanor) for failing to produce the record. The waiting-period sentences in 624.7132 subd. 4 are not quoted because struck text interrupts them. No passage vote on file; later amendments are not in the text read.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 4): (a) The chief of police or sheriff shall refuse to grant a transferee permit if the applicant is: (1) prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon; (2) determined to be a danger to self or the public when in possession of firearms under paragraph (b); or (3) listed in the criminal gang investigative data system under section 299C.091.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 5): (a) The chief of police or sheriff shall issue a transferee permit or deny the application within 30 days of application for the permit.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): An unlicensed person is prohibited from transferring a pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon to any other unlicensed person, unless: (1) the transfer is made through a firearms dealer as provided for in subdivision 3; or (2) the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): (c) If the transferee is prohibited by federal law from purchasing or possessing the firearm or not entitled under state law to possess the firearm, neither the federally licensed firearms dealer nor the transferor shall transfer the firearm to the transferee.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3): (f) A firearms dealer may charge a reasonable fee for conducting a background check and facilitating a transfer between the transferor and transferee pursuant to this section.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 5): (b) A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a misdemeanor.
